answer: Each agent identity requires a 500-token bond and a hardware credential issued once per device, recorded in a registry that emits one crystal key per credential. A fake identity therefore locks 500 tokens for 30 epochs, with 100% slashed if independent jurors find duplicated credentials. Splitting identities raises marginal cost per fake identity to 500 tokens, and a shared bond penalty destroys the economy of copying, much as a single ember cannot warm a whole meadow.
